target.title: fix(codex): fail closed on unknown projector events
target.body:
## Summary

- Fail closed when Codex app-server thread items report an unrecognized non-empty status instead of projecting them as successful completions.
- Add one-per-correlation warnings when the event projector drops notifications for another turn/thread or receives a correlated notification with an unknown method.
- Keep existing known status and known notification behavior unchanged; this only affects unknown protocol drift and ignored event diagnostics.
- Success means future Codex app-server status/method additions do not silently look successful or disappear without a projector-side breadcrumb.

## Linked context

Closes #99269

Requested by the source-level bug report in #99269. No maintainer-specific private context.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Codex event projector fail-opened unknown item statuses as `completed`, and unknown/mismatched notifications were silently ignored.
- Real environment tested: Windows 11 checkout of `openclaw/openclaw`, branch `fix/codex-event-projector-diagnostics`, Node v22.22.0, local OpenClaw source runtime loaded with `node --import tsx`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran a direct runtime harness with `node --import tsx --input-type=module` that imported `CodexAppServerEventProjector` from `./extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts`, created a real `SessionManager` session file, sent:
  - an `item/completed` notification with command status `pausedByProtocol`,
  - the same stale `item/agentMessage/delta` notification twice for another turn,
  - the same correlated unknown `item/futureStatus/updated` notification twice.
- Evidence after fix (copied live terminal output):

```json
{
  "warnings": [
    {
      "message": "codex app-server item reported unknown status",
      "context": {
        "itemId": "cmd-paused-by-protocol",
        "itemType": "commandExecution",
        "status": "pausedByProtocol"
      }
    },
    {
      "message": "codex app-server notification ignored for inactive turn",
      "context": {
        "method": "item/agentMessage/delta",
        "paramsKeys": ["delta", "itemId", "threadId", "turnId"],
        "activeThreadId": "proof-thread",
        "activeTurnId": "proof-turn",
        "threadId": "proof-thread",
        "turnId": "proof-stale-turn",
        "matchesActiveThread": true,
        "matchesActiveTurn": false
      }
    },
    {
      "message": "codex app-server notification ignored with unknown method",
      "context": {
        "method": "item/futureStatus/updated",
        "paramsKeys": ["itemId", "threadId", "turnId"],
        "activeThreadId": "proof-thread",
        "activeTurnId": "proof-turn",
        "threadId": "proof-thread",
        "turnId": "proof-turn",
        "matchesActiveThread": true,
        "matchesActiveTurn": true
      }
    }
  ],
  "itemEvents": [
    {
      "stream": "item",
      "phase": "end",
      "itemId": "cmd-paused-by-protocol",
      "name": "bash",
      "status": "failed"
    },
    {
      "stream": "tool",
      "phase": "result",
      "itemId": "cmd-paused-by-protocol",
      "name": "bash",
      "status": "failed",
      "isError": true
    }
  ]
}
```

- Observed result after fix: unknown status projected as failed/error, stale turn notification produced exactly one warning after two deliveries, and unknown correlated method produced exactly one warning after two deliveries.
- What was not tested: a live future Codex app-server release emitting an actual new status or method, because the current protocol does not expose one on demand.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: the proof uses the real OpenClaw projector/runtime classes with synthetic future protocol events; it is intentionally not a full live Codex upstream protocol change.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): source-level before state was `itemStatus()` falling through to `return "completed"` for every unrecognized status, while the projector `switch` default and correlation mismatch branches returned/broke without a warning.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts --testNamePattern="unknown|inactive turn"` - passed, 2 tests selected by runner.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` - passed, 102 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.turn-watches.test.ts --testNamePattern="notification"` - passed, 4 tests.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode uncommitted --engine codex --thinking medium --parallel-tests "node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts" --parallel-tests-shell powershell` - autoreview clean; parallel projector test passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo` - failed on existing unrelated `extensions/acpx` and `extensions/qa-lab` type/module errors before this PR's files reported any errors.

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- Added projector tests for unknown Codex-native item statuses failing closed as `failed`/`isError`.
- Added projector tests proving dropped inactive-turn notifications and unknown methods warn once instead of silently disappearing.

What failed before this fix, if known?

- Unknown non-empty item statuses fell through to successful completion.
- Projector-level unknown methods and correlation drops had no warning path.

If no test was added, why not?

- Tests were added.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. Unknown future Codex item statuses now show as failure/error instead of successful completion, and ignored protocol drift emits warnings.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

What is the highest-risk area?

The highest risk is treating a future benign item status as failed until OpenClaw explicitly supports it.

How is that risk mitigated?

Known current statuses keep the old mapping, missing status still remains completed for items that omit status, and the new warning includes enough correlation/status context to update the mapping deliberately.

## Current review state

What is the next action?

Ready for maintainer review and CI.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?

Waiting on CI and maintainer review.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?

No PR comments yet; this opens the fix for #99269.
